tempo.label: Tempo mode
tempo.mode_tooltip: Beat evidence is detected by Beat This final0; tempo publication is controlled by the selected mode. Follow source: write a phase-bounded Tempo Map, prefer bar-aligned changes when meter evidence is reliable, and reject beat jitter plus half/double-time errors. Auto: write the one detected global BPM. Manual: keep musical ticks from the same beat grid and use the selected output BPM.
tempo.custom_tooltip: Manual BPM accepts 30–300 BPM. The MIDI uses that one tempo and preserves the musical ticks established at the detected BPM, so playback speed changes by manual BPM ÷ detected BPM; notes are not quantized, filtered, or reconstructed.

muscriptor_result.playback_progress_tooltip: MIDI-master playback progress; dragging seeks MIDI and source audio together
muscriptor_result.export_bpm_tooltip: Project BPM is written to the Standard MIDI File conductor track with the detected meter. Events retain the detected-tempo musical ticks, so file duration changes by project BPM / detected BPM while notes remain unquantized. Enable tempo-map import in a DAW. MuseScore 3/4 may re-beat-track unquantized human performance and replace the displayed notation tempo; that value is generated by MuseScore's importer and does not mean the file tempo was ignored by compliant MIDI hosts
muscriptor_result.playback_speed_tooltip: The playback rate represented by project BPM / detected BPM. Changing this rate updates project BPM and affects linked source/MIDI audition and the downloaded MIDI; note content remains unchanged

muscriptor_result.editor_help: Marquee-select or Ctrl/Shift-click multiple notes. Ctrl+X/C/V cuts, copies and pastes; Ctrl+B or Ctrl+D duplicates right; Alt+Q or Ctrl+U quantizes starts and durations using the current scope and grid (all tracks by default). Arrows move, Shift+Up/Down transposes an octave, Shift+Left/Right changes length, and Ctrl+Up/Down changes velocity. Hold Alt while dragging to bypass snap.
